claims.title: San hunter-gatherers of the Namib
claims.summary: The San, among the oldest human populations on Earth, ranged across the Namib and its margins for tens of thousands of years, hunting, gathering and recording their world in rock art.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-25000bce-san-hunter-gatherers-of-the-namib, claim TL:NAM:event:25000bce:san-hunter-gatherers-of-the-namib, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The engravings of Twyfelfontein
claims.summary: San artists pecked thousands of petroglyphs into the sandstone at Twyfelfontein over roughly two thousand years, depicting animals and tracks bound up with hunter-gatherer ritual; the site was inscribed by UNESCO in 2007.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-2000bce-the-engravings-of-twyfelfontein, claim TL:NAM:event:2000bce:the-engravings-of-twyfelfontein, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Khoekhoe and Damara herders
claims.summary: Khoekhoe pastoralists, including the Nama, and the Damara established themselves across central and southern Namibia, herding cattle and sheep and speaking Khoekhoe click languages.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-500bce-khoekhoe-and-damara-herders, claim TL:NAM:event:500bce:khoekhoe-and-damara-herders, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bantu-speaking peoples settle the north
claims.summary: Over the past fifteen hundred years Bantu-speaking Ovambo, Kavango and Herero peoples migrated into the north and centre, bringing iron-working, agriculture and cattle pastoralism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-500-bantu-speaking-peoples-settle-the-north, claim TL:NAM:event:500:bantu-speaking-peoples-settle-the-north, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Diogo Cão reaches the coast
claims.summary: The Portuguese navigator Diogo Cão landed on the Namib coast and raised a stone cross at Cape Cross; the waterless, harbourless shore — later the Skeleton Coast — long deterred European settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1485-diogo-cao-reaches-the-coast, claim TL:NAM:event:1485:diogo-cao-reaches-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jonker Afrikaner and the Orlam
claims.summary: Jonker Afrikaner led his Orlam followers north into the central highlands, founding a settlement at Windhoek around 1840 and building a mounted, gun-armed state that dominated the interior until 1861.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1823-jonker-afrikaner-and-the-orlam, claim TL:NAM:event:1823:jonker-afrikaner-and-the-orlam, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain annexes Walvis Bay
claims.summary: Britain annexed Walvis Bay, the territory's only deep-water harbour, creating an enclave that would remain in South African hands long after the rest of the country, until 1994.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1878-britain-annexes-walvis-bay, claim TL:NAM:event:1878:britain-annexes-walvis-bay, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Germany declares a protectorate
claims.summary: Following Adolf Lüderitz's purchase at Angra Pequena in 1883, Bismarck declared a German protectorate over the territory in 1884, founding the colony of German South West Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1884-germany-declares-a-protectorate, claim TL:NAM:event:1884:germany-declares-a-protectorate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Herero uprising begins
claims.summary: Herero forces under paramount chief Samuel Maharero rose against German colonial rule, killing more than a hundred settlers and triggering a brutal German military response.

sources.label: Timeline of the German and Herero, Nama War and Genocide

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1904-the-herero-uprising-begins, claim TL:NAM:event:1904:the-herero-uprising-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Waterberg
claims.summary: German forces under Lothar von Trotha defeated the main Herero force at Waterberg and drove the survivors into the Omaheke desert, where thousands, including women and children, died of thirst.

sources.label: The Massacre of the Herero and Nama: A colonial laboratory for genocide?

claims.title: Von Trotha's extermination order
claims.summary: Von Trotha issued the Vernichtungsbefehl, ordering that every Herero within the colony, armed or not, be shot; a second order against the Nama followed in April 1905, opening a war of extermination.

sources.label: Commemorating the Genocide of the Herero and Nama
The Massacre of the Herero and Nama: A colonial laboratory for genocide?

claims.title: Shark Island and the concentration camps
claims.summary: Herero and Nama survivors were imprisoned in concentration camps, most notoriously on Shark Island at Lüderitz, where up to 80 percent of prisoners died; by 1908 tens of thousands of Herero and Nama had perished in what is widely called the first genocide of the twentieth century.

sources.label: Commemorating the Genocide of the Herero and Nama

claims.title: South Africa conquers the colony
claims.summary: South African forces invaded German South West Africa during the First World War and forced the German garrison to surrender, beginning seventy-five years of South African rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1915-south-africa-conquers-the-colony, claim TL:NAM:event:1915:south-africa-conquers-the-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: League of Nations mandate
claims.summary: The League of Nations granted South Africa a mandate to administer the territory as a trust for its inhabitants; South Africa instead governed it as a near-province, settling white farmers and suppressing African political life.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1920-league-of-nations-mandate, claim TL:NAM:event:1920:league-of-nations-mandate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: South Africa refuses UN trusteeship
claims.summary: After the founding of the United Nations, South Africa refused to place the territory under UN trusteeship and sought to annex it, beginning a long international dispute over its status.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1946-south-africa-refuses-un-trusteeship, claim TL:NAM:event:1946:south-africa-refuses-un-trusteeship, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Old Location shootings
claims.summary: Police killed about a dozen residents of Windhoek's Old Location protesting forced removal to Katutura township, an atrocity that helped galvanise the nationalist movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1959-the-old-location-shootings, claim TL:NAM:event:1959:the-old-location-shootings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of SWAPO
claims.summary: The South West African People's Organisation was founded under Sam Nujoma as successor to the Ovamboland People's Organisation, becoming the leading movement for Namibian independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1960-founding-of-swapo, claim TL:NAM:event:1960:founding-of-swapo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Armed struggle begins at Omugulugwombashe
claims.summary: SWAPO's military wing, PLAN, fought South African forces at Omugulugwombashe, marking the start of the armed liberation war and of South Africa's long Border War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1966-armed-struggle-begins-at-omugulugwombashe, claim TL:NAM:event:1966:armed-struggle-begins-at-omugulugwombashe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN revokes the mandate
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly terminated South Africa's mandate over the territory, declaring its continued administration illegal, and later renamed the territory Namibia in 1968.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1966-un-revokes-the-mandate, claim TL:NAM:event:1966:un-revokes-the-mandate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ICJ rules the occupation illegal
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice held that South Africa's continued presence in Namibia was illegal and that it was obliged to withdraw its administration immediately.

sources.label: Legal Consequences for States of the Continued Presence of South Africa in Namibia (1971 Advisory Opinion)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1971-icj-rules-the-occupation-illegal, claim TL:NAM:event:1971:icj-rules-the-occupation-illegal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Security Council Resolution 435
claims.summary: The UN Security Council adopted Resolution 435, setting out a plan for a ceasefire and UN-supervised elections that would eventually frame Namibia's transition to independence.

sources.label: The UN's role in Namibian Independence

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1978-security-council-resolution-435, claim TL:NAM:event:1978:security-council-resolution-435, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN-supervised elections
claims.summary: With Resolution 435 in force from 1 April 1989 under the UN Transition Assistance Group (UNTAG), Namibians elected a Constituent Assembly that SWAPO won with about 57 percent of the vote; the assembly drafted a democratic constitution adopted in February 1990.

sources.label: The UN's role in Namibian Independence

claims.title: Independence and Nujoma's inauguration
claims.summary: At midnight on 21 March 1990 the Namibian flag was raised in Windhoek, ending South African rule, and Sam Nujoma was sworn in as the first president of the independent Republic of Namibia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1990-independence-and-nujoma-s-inauguration, claim TL:NAM:event:1990:independence-and-nujoma-s-inauguration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reincorporation of Walvis Bay
claims.summary: South Africa transferred the port enclave of Walvis Bay and the offshore islands to Namibia, completing the country's territory and giving it sovereignty over its only deep-water harbour.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-1994-reincorporation-of-walvis-bay, claim TL:NAM:event:1994:reincorporation-of-walvis-bay, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First peaceful transfer of power
claims.summary: Sam Nujoma stepped down after fifteen years and was succeeded as president by Hifikepunye Pohamba, the first of several peaceful handovers within SWAPO governments.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-2005-first-peaceful-transfer-of-power, claim TL:NAM:event:2005:first-peaceful-transfer-of-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Germany acknowledges the genocide
claims.summary: Germany formally recognised the 1904–1908 killings of the Herero and Nama as genocide and pledged development funding, though many descendants rejected the terms as inadequate.

sources.label: Commemorating the Genocide of the Herero and Nama

claims.title: First woman president elected
claims.summary: Namibians elected Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, a veteran of the liberation struggle, as the country's first woman president, extending SWAPO's continuous tenure since independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Namibia: From the San and Khoekhoe of the Namib and the rock art of Twyfelfontein, through the German colonial genocide of the Herero and Nama, decades of South African rule and apartheid, and the long liberation struggle, to independence under Sam Nujoma on 21 March 1990.", terralore.co/country/NAM/chronicle#ev-2024-first-woman-president-elected, claim TL:NAM:event:2024:first-woman-president-elected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
